## Summary

Apps on Devices runs Android POS applications on Stripe smart readers. Both the May 1 and November 7, 2026 guides describe access for eligible merchants with an Android POS app or resources to build one. Eligible users on standard card-present pricing pay no extra cost. Contact Stripe Sales for eligibility and pricing assessment, or use the support form if you have no sales representative. Stripe handles payments and compliance through the Android or React Native Terminal SDK.

## Integration Modes

1. **POS on the reader.** The device starts in the merchant POS app. The Stripe Reader app takes the foreground during payment, then returns primary control to the POS app.
2. **POS and reader on separate devices.** The consumer-facing Android app runs on the smart reader and supports payment. The merchant manages communication between the apps over TCP/IP.

## Upload and Device Requirements

- **APK size.** Standard Stripe API uploads have a 200 MB limit in both captures. November documents a separate private preview for uploads up to 300 MB. The email form requests access and does not enable it immediately. See November raw lines 50–64.
- **Storage and Android environment.** Stripe manages updates over the air and caps app storage on the device at 8 GB. SmartPOS OS is based on AOSP. Google Play Services, notifications and a user-accessible home screen are unavailable. Production devices disable USB, ADB and debugging.
- **Development hardware.** May describes using a DevKit for development. November explicitly requires a DevKit for Apps on Devices development and testing and documents ordering up to five DevKits per user through Dashboard Readers. Operators with only a production reader can accept payments through a server-driven integration or use standalone mode on a supported reader.
- **T600 (November).** Without a main battery, app termination is more likely to leave partial writes. Apps must be able to handle these in data stores, logs and downloads. Each T600 DevKit includes the T-bridge required for DevKit power and data. See November raw lines 86–96.
- **Specifications by reader.** The May S700/S710 table lists Snapdragon 665 (QCM6125), 4 GB RAM, 64 GB storage, Android 10, 1080×1920 and 420 dpi. November routes to device-specific specifications for T600, S700/S710 and Verifone. See May raw lines 53–65 and November lines 66–72.

## Permissions and Connect

SmartPOS OS grants allowed manifest permissions during installation without a runtime prompt. Apps requesting permissions outside the allowlist are rejected. November adds `android.permission.CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE` to the documented allowlist (raw lines 98–116). Camera, Bluetooth and location are experimental. The overview scopes NFC to payments for Apps on Devices. See the separate [[source-stripe-terminal-collect-nfc-data]] route for Terminal’s tapped-data private-preview evidence and integration scope.

For direct charges, a single platform must control the connected account. Platforms deploy apps only to singly controlled connected accounts, with `controller.is_controller = true` documented as the qualification.

## App Lifecycle

Build and test, prepare for app review, submit, deploy to selected devices, then monitor. The May deploy step points to the [Deploy API](https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/apps-on-devices/deploy-with-API.md). November points to [[source-stripe-terminal-apps-on-devices-deploy-dashboard|Dashboard deployment]]. The [[source-stripe-terminal-apps-on-devices-deploy-api|separate API deployment guide]] documents private-preview access through Stripe Support.

terminal-features-apps-on-devices-overvi.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/apps-on-devices/overview, the revised source-stripe-terminal-apps-on-devices.md preserves the two Android POS architectures and updates the developer limits and prerequisites. The merchant needs an existing Android POS app or resources to build one and requests eligibility through sales or support. Standard card-present pricing carries no extra Apps on Devices cost for eligible users. Stripe handles payments and compliance with the Android or React Native Terminal SDK. One device boots into the merchant POS app, switches the primary app to Stripe Reader during the transaction, and returns primary control to the POS after it finishes. A separate-device POS communicates over merchant-managed TCP/IP with the consumer-facing Android app on the smart reader (old raw lines 8-22, old raw lines 33-42, new raw lines 9-23, new raw lines 34-43). The developer builds/tests on a DevKit, prepares for review, submits, deploys to selected readers and monitors. The standard Stripe API APK upload max remains 200 MB, and November documents a separate private preview for up to 300 MB where the request form does not activate access immediately. November adds a five-DevKit order limit per user and T600 no-main-battery/partial-write and T-bridge requirements (old raw lines 49-69, old raw lines 71-83, new raw lines 50-76, new raw lines 80-100). The OS grants allowed manifest permissions at install without runtime prompts and rejects over-allowlist apps, with camera, Bluetooth and location experimental. Direct charges require one controlling platform, and the deploy eligibility section preserves the single-platform controller.is_controller=true qualification (old raw lines 81-87, old raw lines 128-134, new raw lines 98-105, new raw lines 146-152).
terminal-features-apps-on-devices-overvi.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/features/apps-on-devices/overview, source-stripe-terminal-apps-on-devices.md records the substantive November updates alongside the May full capture. November 7 retains the ordinary 200 MB Stripe API cap, adds a 300 MB private preview with an email request and no immediate enablement, and makes the DevKit requirement explicit. Preserve its per-user cap, production-reader server-driven or supported standalone alternatives, and the T600's partial-write risk without a main battery and included T-bridge for DevKit power/data. The November allowlist also newly includes CHANGE_WIFI_MULTICAST_STATE, without claiming tested capability from permission alone (old raw lines 49-51, old raw lines 73-83, old raw lines 87-102, new raw lines 50-64, new raw lines 80-100, new raw lines 104-120). The two integration diagrams and numbered lifecycle formatting changed presentation. The deploy step now links to Dashboard, without changing the lifecycle phase or proving API retirement. Preserve the separately documented API private-preview route. The May inline S700/S710 specs remain dated evidence. November routes specifications to T600, S700/S710 and Verifone device pages (old raw lines 18-22, old raw lines 33-43, old raw lines 53-65, new raw lines 19-23, new raw lines 34-44, new raw lines 66-76). The proposed reciprocal stripe-terminal-apps-on-devices and stripe-terminal routes qualify the APK ceiling and the dedicated concept’s deployment steps. The Apps on Devices NFC restriction and experimental capabilities remain scoped to this product, with a separate Terminal tapped-data private-preview route (old raw lines 128-134, new raw lines 146-152).
